title: Regulus Returns to Carthage
text:
During the First Punic War the Roman general Marcus Atilius Regulus invaded Africa and was defeated and captured by the Carthaginians in 255 BC.

According to the story told by Cicero and later Roman writers, some years later the Carthaginians sent him to Rome with their envoys to arrange an exchange of prisoners, after making him swear that he would return to Carthage if the exchange failed. In Rome, Cicero says, Regulus refused to speak in the Senate as a citizen at first, since he considered himself a prisoner. Then he argued against the exchange. The Carthaginian prisoners were young and capable commanders, he said, while he was old and worn out. Returning them would harm Rome.

The Senate followed his advice. His family and friends begged him to stay. Regulus kept his oath and went back to Carthage, where, the story says, he was put to death by cruel tortures.

Cicero held him up in On Duties as the model of a man who kept his word to an enemy because an oath is an oath. The poet Horace describes him pushing through the crowd of relatives who tried to hold him back.
lesson: Keep your word even when breaking it would be easy and no one could force you. Promises kept at a cost are what make trust possible.
source: Cicero, De Officiis, Book 3, chapters 99 to 115; Horace, Odes, Book 3, Ode 5
caveat: Polybius does not mention the embassy or the torture, and many historians consider them Roman legend.
